problem: VLN datasets lack higher-level, linguistically grounded annotations of navigation concepts, so cross-modal alignment between instruction text and visual observations stays opaque. Prior work using dependency parses relies on noisy off-the-shelf parsers and heuristics, which hurts reproducibility and interpretability.
motivation: Moving from black-box end-to-end VLN models to grounded, interpretable ones needs data linking language concepts to navigation actions and visual inputs. Manual annotation at this scale is unrealistic, so an automatic silver-annotation pipeline that needs little human effort is required.
key_idea: Define four cognitively inspired navigation concepts (Situate Yourself, Move along a Path, Change Direction, Change Region), silver-annotate them in R2R/RxR instructions via root-verb phrases from a constituency parse, and align them with video clips using RxR word timestamps.
insight: A small taxonomy of 81 root navigation verbs, with their syntactic children as spans, covers most instruction content: 236K annotations, with human-verified span and label accuracy above 95%. Video alignment depends on RxR word-timestamp accuracy; extending the extraction window by 5% raised exact-match clips from 73.63% to 88.62%. A fine-tuned DistilBERT tagger recovers the silver labels exactly on 96.53% of concepts, while GPT-4o with 3-shot prompting reaches 82.12%, so the pipeline remains better than the LLM.
method: Concept taxonomy: four classes (SIT, MOVE, CD, CR) motivated by place cells, head-direction cells, boundary cells and locomotion/paths (Lynch).

Root verb extraction: Stanza constituency parse and spaCy pipeline over 30,815 R2R/RxR-CE train instructions gave 348 root verbs; humans filtered them to 81 navigation verbs mapped to the four concepts.
Phrase retrieval: 244,894 verb phrases (root verb plus syntactic children) were retrieved and cleaned (e.g., removing phrases with two root verbs), giving 236,316 concept annotations.

Video-clip alignment: RxR word timestamps and pose traces are used to render RGB-D frames in Habitat/Matterport3D (1 in 10 frames, 320x240). Missing timestamps are interpolated, phrases are split into words, and the end window is extended; this gives 2.7M frames for 19,074 instructions.
Navigation Concept Classifier: DistilBERT-base-uncased fine-tuned for BIO token tagging into 4 concepts plus O (lr 1e-5, 6 epochs, 30,629 instructions).
GPT-4o few-shot tagger: a prompt with 3 annotated instructions asks GPT-4o to tag every token of 190 unseen gold instructions (1,521 concepts).

setting.backbone: DistilBERT-base-uncased (fine-tuned) for the concept classifier; GPT-4o (frozen, few-shot) as comparison; Stanza/spaCy parsers for annotation
setting.training_data: NAVCON silver annotations on 30,629 R2R-CE/RxR-CE English train instructions
setting.observation: text instructions (concept tagging); RGB-D frames rendered from RxR pose traces (320x240) for video clips
setting.action_space: not applicable (annotation/dataset paper; no navigation agent)

numbers_note: No navigation benchmark results; only annotation quality and concept-tagging accuracy (classifier 96.53% exact concept+phrase match; GPT-4o 82.12%). Not standard VLN metrics.
results: NAVCON provides 236,316 concept annotations over 30,815 R2R/RxR instructions and 2.7M aligned frames. Human evaluation found 95.49% of spans and 95.82% of labels correct. The DistilBERT classifier reaches 96.53% exact concept and phrase match, and 3-shot GPT-4o reaches 82.12% on 190 unseen instructions (1,521 concepts).
limitations: Relies on the Stanza constituency parser, which is imperfect, and on a limited verb list; the annotations are silver, not gold.
Video alignment is limited by inaccurate RxR word-timestamps and Habitat rendering artifacts; only RxR has timestamps, and 44% of movement clips initially showed no pose change.
No downstream VLN agent is trained or evaluated with NAVCON, so its usefulness for navigation is not shown; classifier scores are measured against the silver labels from the same pipeline.
